_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.gis.gisterrain` persists exactly two scalars and derives its mesh child handle from them, so both mutation kinds are root-scalar setters with an indirect, content-addressed effect. Semio-NATIVE, no oracle; the geospatial libraries surveyed and declined are named below.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: `s.gis.gisterrain` is a semio-NATIVE artifact — `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, read by nobody else — and it persists exactly two fields: an `f64` vertical exaggeration and a raw `imported_features_json` string that is `map:in`'s insertion point. A third slot, `mesh`, is not persisted content but a CONTENT-ADDRESSED child handle derived from those two fields alone. The geospatial ecosystem's real libraries were surveyed and DECLINED: `geo`/`geo-types` and `geojson` model geometry and features, and `gdal` models raster/vector datasets, but this vocabulary's two verbs do not edit geometry at all — `change-exaggeration` scales a display factor and `change-imported-features` swaps an opaque JSON payload the artifact never interprets — so a geometry library put in the position of judging them would be adjudicating a field it cannot see. Evidence is the two committed specification vectors (`raises-the-exaggeration-from-one-to-two-and-a-half`, `imports-a-single-harbor-position-descriptor`) plus the inverse law, which here is unusually sharp: both inverses are BASE-derived value restores, and because `mesh` is content-addressed off `(exaggeration, imported_features_json)`, an implementation that forgot to re-derive the handle after undoing leaves a stale `childId` behind and fails.
